item.title: Optimization for One, Feasibility for Most: Decoupling Optimization from Feasibility in Chance-Constrained Programs
item.description: arXiv:2610.19027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chance-constrained stochastic programs (CCSPs) require solutions that satisfy uncertain constraints with high probability. Standard approaches either embed scenarios directly into optimization by considering sample average approximation (SAA)-based reformulations, growing prohibitively expensive and often failing to find feasible solutions; or employ conservative reformulations that guarantee feasibility but sacrifice objective quality by design. We propose ACCESS (Adaptive Chance-Constrained Exploration via Structured Sampling), a structured sampling framework that decouples optimization from feasibility evaluation. First, high-quality candidate solutions are generated by solving many inexpensive single-scenario subproblems, avoiding sampling directly in the constrained high-dimensional solution space. Second, feasibility is assessed separately via large-scale batched simulation over a massive number of scenarios, which is naturally amenable to GPU parallelism. That reduces the search from a high-dimensional solution space to a two-dimensional parameter space controlling conservatism and scenario diversity; while concentrating on candidates near the feasibility boundary, where high-quality feasible solutions lie. We also introduce a variant, ACCESS($\delta$), which provides certified feasibility guarantees with probability $1-\delta$. Experiments across three benchmark classes and five scenario distributions show that ACCESS matches or exceeds the best objective found by any method in nearly every setting, while ACCESS($\delta$) is empirically feasible on every instance. The conservative reformulations remain several percent worse in objective, and SAA is frequently infeasible while taking an order of magnitude longer on the harder benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Justin Dumouchelle, Shunyu Yao, Beste Basciftci, Thiago Serra

item.title: First-order Optimization Methods with Generalized Smoothness for Low-rank Matrix Factorization
item.description: arXiv:2610.19059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies several first-order methods for low-rank matrix minimization in the Burer--Monteiro form, where the target matrix is represented as the product of a nonnegative factor matrix and its transpose. Such a factorization destroys convexity of the objective function and global Lipschitz continuity of the gradient. We prove that for a quadratic objective function that is strongly convex only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, the Burer-Monteiro factorized objective possesses generalized smoothness with a fractional exponent 2/3. For a quadratic objective, the generalized smoothness property requires positive definiteness of the operator A only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, which relaxes the assumptions of Dragomir et al. On this basis, three methods are proposed: an adaptive gradient descent method with Armijo backtracking; an unconstrained SafeAdam method combining the Adam direction with a descent-angle certificate and a fallback to the normalized gradient; and a certified projected version for the nonnegativity constraint. Global convergence and explicit convergence rates for the proposed methods have been proved. The obtained convergence rate is better than the convergence rate of ordinary unaccelerated gradient descent in the case of a sufficiently large gradient. In the small-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of square-root type, and the corresponding complexity scales as the inverse square of the desired accuracy. In the large-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of three-quarters type, and the corresponding complexity is proportional to the inverse of the accuracy raised to the power of 4/3. Experiments on SymNMF using the TDT2, Reuters and CBCL datasets, which are standard benchmarks for document and image clustering, show that the methods match or outperform Dyn-NoLips without tuning the relative-smoothness kernel parameters.
item.dc:creator: A. V. Bidanets, F. S. Stonyakin

item.title: Aggregated Column Generation for Two-Stage Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programs
item.description: arXiv:2610.19181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation applied to two-stage stochastic mixed-integer programs (SMIP) has been shown empirically to yield a formulation with strong bounds that can be solved via column generation. However, the time to solve the restricted master problem grows significantly with the number of scenarios due to the increasing number of nonanticipativity constraints (NACs). Moreover, the associated high-dimensional dual space can cause the dual multipliers to oscillate between iterations, further slowing convergence. We propose an aggregated column generation framework for solving a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation. Applied to SMIP, this method partitions the NACs into groups and replaces each group with a weighted surrogate constraint, leading to a reduced size and providing implicit stabilization by restricting the dual space. While aggregation leads to a relaxation, we develop two strategies for recovering the standard Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation bound. The first iteratively refines the partition by splitting groups that contain violated constraints. The second keeps the partition fixed and adaptively updates the aggregation weights. We prove convergence of the two approaches and study their computational performance on two benchmark problem classes.
item.dc:creator: Harshit Kothari, James Luedtke, Luke Marshall

item.title: Large-Step Last-Iterate Convergence of Random-Reshuffling Stochastic Gradient Descent
item.description: arXiv:2610.19444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Random reshuffling stochastic gradient descent (RR-SGD) is widely used for finite-sum optimization in machine learning. For convex $L$-smooth components, recent work establishes convergence guarantees for an averaged iterate with component stepsizes as large as order $1/L$. However, the final iterate is a natural output in practice, and existing last-iterate guarantees in this setting require stepsizes that scale inversely with the number of components $n$. We establish an expected objective-gap bound for the last iterate of standard RR-SGD on unconstrained problems with a constant component stepsize satisfying $0<\eta\lesssim 1/(L(1 + \log(nK)))$, where $K$ is the number of epochs. By retaining the sampling bias at random comparison points, we remove the explicit $1/n$ factor from the stepsize restriction. Combined with existing small-step bounds, our result matches the corresponding averaged-iterate convergence rate up to logarithmic factors.
item.dc:creator: Zijun Chen, Zihan Zhang

item.title: Convergence Rates of Factorized Gradient Descent for Overparameterized Asymmetric Matrix Sensing with Balancing Regularization
item.description: arXiv:2610.19477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study factorized gradient descent (FGD) for overparameterized asymmetric matrix sensing with the balancing regularizer $\frac18\|L^\top L-R^\top R\|_F^2$. An exact indefinite lifting of the population objective decomposes the dynamics of FGD into positive, negative, and null spectral subspaces. The first two components have linear restoring terms, whereas the null component contracts only quadratically. For independent isotropic sub-Gaussian sensing matrices and independent centered sub-Gaussian noise with scale proxy $\sigma$, we prove the local bound \[ \|L_tR_t^\top-X^\star\|_2 \lesssim\max\left\{\frac{1}{\eta t+1/\sigma_r}, \kappa\sigma\sqrt{\frac{d_1+d_2}{n}}\right\}, \] under a sufficiently small initialization error, the number of linear measurements $n\gtrsim\kappa^2(d_1+d_2)\max\{k^2,\sigma^2/\sigma_r^2\}$, and step size $\eta\lesssim\sigma_1^{-1}$. Here $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_r$ are the largest and smallest nonzero singular values of the target $X^\star\in \mathbb{R}^{d_1\times d_2}$ respectively, and $\kappa=\sigma_1/\sigma_r$. Furthermore, a population trajectory was constructed to have tight product error $\Theta(1/t)$. These results provide a local rate characterization for ordinary gradient descent for overparameterized asymmetric matrix sensing with balancing regularizer.
item.dc:creator: Yongjun Chen, Jiaming Zhang, Liping Zhang

item.title: The Big Match under translation-invariant charges
item.description: arXiv:2610.19646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two-player zero-sum stochastic games in which a stream of stage payoffs is evaluated by a translation-invariant charge on the set of stages. Every patient valuation, that is, every diffuse charge that obeys the time value of money principle, is translation-invariant, and by Mertens and Neyman each player has, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a strategy that is $\varepsilon$-optimal for all patient valuations simultaneously. We show that this robustness breaks down for translation-invariant charges. In the Big Match with $0$--$1$ payoffs, whose uniform value is $1/2$, every strategy of Player 1 is worthless: for every strategy of Player 1 and every $\delta>0$, Player 2 has a pure reply, and there is a translation-invariant charge under which Player 1's payoff is less than $\delta$. Consequently, the Big Match has no value with respect to all translation-invariant charges. This contrasts with finite Markov decision processes, where every stationary Blackwell optimal strategy is optimal for every translation-invariant charge. We pose questions on robust guarantees in general stochastic games and on optimality with respect to a fixed translation-invariant charge.
item.dc:creator: Abraham Neyman

item.title: Time-Inconsistent Singular Dividend Control with Regime Switching and Bankruptcy
item.description: arXiv:2610.19655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies infinite-horizon equilibrium dividend distribution for a firm whose surplus follows a diffusion under observable Markov regime switching and is absorbed at bankruptcy. Dividend payments are modeled as singular controls, and non-exponential discounting leads to time inconsistency. We formulate equilibrium control laws and establish a verification theorem for a general finite-state model with surplus-dependent coefficients. For a two-state model with constant positive drifts and volatilities and bi-exponential discounting, we prove the existence of a regime-dependent equilibrium barrier policy for arbitrary positive switching intensities. The policy retains surplus below the prevailing regime's threshold and distributes any excess immediately. Numerical experiments examine how shareholder patience and economic conditions affect dividend decisions. Over the parameter ranges considered, greater discount-rate dispersion at a fixed initial average rate raises both barriers, while switching speed can generate nonmonotone responses and reverse their ordering.
item.dc:creator: Xiaochen Chen, Guohui Guan, Zongxia Liang, Xiaodong Luo

item.title: On Completely Positive and Semidefinite Programs for Moment Bounds on Maximum of Random Quadratics
item.description: arXiv:2610.19684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Completely positive programs are known to provide an exact representation to several NP-hard optimization problems. In this work, we look at the maximum of random quadratic functions and compute the maximum expected value over ambiguity sets defined with moment and support information. We propose exact completely positive programs and semidefinite programs when the random variables are Bernoulli, nonnegative and unrestricted in support. Our experimental study demonstrates the utility of these formulations.
item.dc:creator: Buse Unluturk, Divya Padmanabhan, Karthik Natarajan

item.title: Safety stock calculation with heteroscedastic, autocorrelated and heavy-tailed forecast errors, an adaptive parametric method.e
item.description: arXiv:2610.19829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops and validates an adaptive parametric method for sizing safety stock when forecast errors are autocorrelated, heteroscedastic, asymmetric, and heavy-tailed. Using four years of weekly forecasts from a fast-moving consumer goods company, the analysis identifies substantial positive autocorrelation, departures from normality, systematic forecast optimism, and heterogeneous relationships between forecast volume and error variance. The proposed method integrates several corrections into a modular, sequential safety-stock architecture. It constructs cumulative forecast errors over the operational action period, selects an SKU-specific parametric distribution, and determines a baseline protection point using an expected-shortage condition consistent with the target beta fill rate. A forecast-scaled module adjusts dispersion when error variance depends on forecast volume, while a Cycle-End Exposure safeguard limits within-cycle shortage risk when large replenishment lots increase exposure. Performance is evaluated through discrete-event simulation against the company's current method. The proposed method reduces average inventory by 9.9% and maximum inventory by 19.5%, with no statistically significant deterioration in beta fill rate or average stockout duration. The proportion of weeks without stockouts declines slightly, without evidence of more persistent or operationally severe shortages. The heteroscedasticity module provides selective benefits, with greater service improvements as variance dependence intensifies. The resulting framework is interpretable, adapts to SKU-specific statistical profiles, links distributional features to safety-stock outcomes, and can be integrated into existing ERP environments.
item.dc:creator: Luis Fern\'andez-Palacios, Manuel Ceballos, Yolanda Mu\~noz-Oca\~na

item.title: GPU-Accelerated Preprocessing for Large-Scale Linear Programming
item.description: arXiv:2610.19840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GPU-accelerated first-order methods are increasingly effective for solving large-scale linear programs (LPs), yet LP preprocessing remains predominantly CPU-based and can become costly. A key challenge is that dependencies among presolve reductions and frequent modifications to sparse LP data make efficient GPU parallelization difficult. To address this challenge, we develop GPU-Preprocessor, a GPU-native LP preprocessing framework that integrates folding and presolve. To efficiently implement folding on GPUs, we adapt a randomized partition refinement algorithm to LP folding, using sparse matrix-vector products and parallel sorting to construct stable row and column partitions. For presolve, we introduce a new piecewise-linear reformulation rule that exploits underlying convex piecewise-linear structure to obtain sparser LP representations. We also develop a framework that combines phase scheduling with a Scan-Plan-Apply design to coordinate presolve rules and reduce sparse-matrix reconstruction overhead through batched updates. Numerical experiments on three LP benchmark sets show that GPU-Preprocessor achieves greater average problem-size reductions than PSLP and Gurobi Presolve, with SGM10 preprocessing-time speedups of up to $43.9\times$ and $677.7\times$, respectively. Here, SGM10 denotes the shifted geometric mean with a 10-second shift. On the largest tested quadratic assignment problem LP relaxation, these speedups reach $126.3\times$ and $2{,}207.9\times$. When integrated with the GPU-accelerated LP solver HPR-LP, GPU-Preprocessor achieves SGM10 speedups of $2.5\times$ to $5.0\times$ in combined preprocessing and solving time over HPR-LP without preprocessing. The code is available at https://github.com/PolyU-IOR/GPU-Preprocessor.
item.dc:creator: Kaihuang Chen, Jiawei Lu, Defeng Sun, Yancheng Yuan, Guojun Zhang, Xiangyu Zhang, Xinyuan Zhao

item.title: Does Policy Mirror Descent Converge in Policy with Non-Decomposable Mirror Maps? A Counterexample
item.description: arXiv:2610.19853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Policy mirror descent (PMD) refers to a class of policy optimization methods associated with different mirror maps. For a broad class of decomposable Legendre mirror maps encompassing many standard choices, Li and Wei [2026] show that the PMD policy sequence converges to an optimal policy from any admissible initialization under any positive constant step size, even when the optimal policy is not unique. In this note, we provide a counterexample with assistance from OpenAI's GPT-5.6 model, showing that PMD with a non-decomposable Legendre mirror map need not converge in policy.
item.dc:creator: Wenye Li, Ke Wei

item.title: ANOVA approximation for high-dimensional control systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.19858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the data-driven approximation of control-affine systems, where the drift and each control vector field exhibit a low-dimensional structure. While the ANOVA (ANalysis Of VAriance) decomposition is tailored to low-dimensional structures, a straightforward implementation does not exploit control affinity, rendering the approximation computationally expensive. We propose a coupled least squares approach for given state-control samples, whose ansatz is affine linear in the control by construction and can be realized by a preprocessing of the ANOVA index sets. Based on a Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund inequality for the resulting ansatz space, we prove a probabilistic $L_2$-error bound with explicitly given constants. Separate error control on drift and input vector fields renders the approach flexible to, e.\,g., parameter changes. Finally, we numerically illustrate the identification of the coupling structure via global sensitivity indices on discretizations of a nonlinear advection-diffusion equation, the shallow water equations and the viscous Burgers equation.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Kircheis, Daniel Potts, Manuel Schaller, Karl Worthmann

item.title: On the Regularization of Primal-Dual Dynamics in Time-Dependent Nonconvex Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.19916v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study continuous-time primal-dual dynamics for tracking solutions of time-dependent constrained optimization problems. First, for uniformly strongly convex-strongly concave saddle functions, we establish explicit finite-time tracking and additive-disturbance bounds. For convex problems, we then introduce a directional primal regularization, combined with dual Tikhonov regularization, and quantify the resulting optimization bias and constraint violation. For smooth nonconvex problems, we couple a proximal local convexification with a two-time-scale primal-dual flow and obtain a local tracking result under constraint qualification, second-order sufficiency, and temporal regularity. Numerical traffic-signal experiments at a single intersection evaluate the proposed method under vehicle-throughput and pedestrian-aware objectives, comparing it with standard signal-control schemes.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Vaquero, Jorge Cort\'es

item.title: Recursive Gradient Retraction Methods for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization on Stiefel Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.19944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonconvex optimization on Stiefel manifolds underlies many problems in machine learning and deep learning. However, existing stochastic Riemannian retraction methods often rely on stepsizes that require prior knowledge of the gradient Lipschitz constant, a prescribed iteration horizon, or restrictive batch-size choices. We develop {\sf RGR}, a recursive gradient retraction method for stochastic nonconvex optimization on Stiefel manifolds. Instead of recursively updating gradient estimators in changing tangent spaces, {\sf RGR} constructs them in the Euclidean space and subsequently maps them to tangent space, thereby avoiding vector transport. The method comprises three variants: {\sf RGR-SPIDER} for finite-sum optimization and {\sf RGR-SRM} and {\sf RGR-EMA} for online stochastic optimization. {\sf RGR-SPIDER} is Lipschitz-free and horizon-free, as its adaptive stepsize requires neither prior knowledge of the gradient Lipschitz constant nor a prescribed iteration horizon. {\sf RGR-SRM} and {\sf RGR-EMA} are mini-batch and horizon-free methods whose convergence guarantees do not rely on prescribed large batch sizes and whose parameters can be chosen without prior knowledge of the total iteration budget. We show that {\sf RGR-SPIDER} reaches an $\varepsilon$-critical point using $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations and $\mathcal{O}(N+\sqrt{N}\varepsilon^{-2})$ component-gradient evaluations, where $N$ denotes the number of component functions. For the online setting, {\sf RGR-SRM} and {\sf RGR-EMA} achieve iteration complexities of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-4})$, respectively. Experiments on principal component analysis, low-rank matrix completion, and orthogonal convolutional neural networks demonstrate faster empirical convergence than methods that construct recursive gradient estimators directly in Riemannian tangent spaces.
item.dc:creator: Zhijie Yuan, Lei Sun, Ganzhao Yuan

item.title: L1 Minimum Energy Estimation of Positive Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.19976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a novel class of minimum energy estimation problems for positive linear systems with linear costs subject to coupled process and measurement disturbances, where the latter is bounded by the state and the former is bounded by the noise. Through dynamic programming we show that the problem admits explicit solutions. Remarkably, the Luenberger observer structure of the optimal estimator emerges from the optimization itself, with a switching gain that inherits the sparsity of the disturbance constraints, and it is obtained from a differential equation in the finite horizon case. In the infinite horizon case, an algebraic equation characterizes the limit of the finite-horizon solution and yields a stationary estimator with a static gain. We introduce two distinct notions of detectability to characterize when the static gain stabilizes the error dynamics while preserving their positivity, and analyze under which conditions the stationary solution can be formulated as a linear program. We further establish that a disturbance perturbation of finite L1-norm yields an estimation error of finite L1-norm. The framework is illustrated on a large-scale irrigation network.
item.dc:creator: Alba Gurpegui Ram\'on

item.title: New spherical codes by tuning an annealing solver
item.description: arXiv:2610.19988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spherical code problem asks how to place $N$ points on a unit sphere in $D$ dimensions to maximize the smallest distance between two points. It is a non-smooth and non-convex max-min problem, where few problem sizes have known optimal solutions, some have constructions, but most still only have numerically obtained solutions. We use a simple solver, with seven parameters, that anneals a LogSumExp surrogate, minimizes with L-BFGS, applies a random perturbation between anneals, and repeats with no acceptance test until a fixed limit is reached. We search the solver parameters for every instance with $N \le 1024$, $3 \le D \le 32$, and $N > 2D$, a total of 29,670 instances, using 32 parameter trials. We then run the solver for 60 seconds with the best parameters for each instance, without utilizing any symmetries or existing solutions. After enforcing monotonicity of the results and numerically polishing the solutions, we improve the best known code in 4,577 instances. When a single set of solver parameters is used for all instances, with one 60-second episode, the number of improvements is still 3,649. From our records, we find 24 codes with an exact algebraic cosine. Among our ablations, we find that 1) the repeated anneal contributes most to improvements, 2) at our $32 \times 60$-second budget only fitting one parameter per-instance is better than fitting all seven, and 3) good parameters can be predicted from the instance size. We provide the solver code, the fitted parameters, and the codes.
item.dc:creator: Ilmari Vahteristo

item.title: A particle swarm optimization with a reduced-subspace trust-region safeguard for contact-rich controller tuning
item.description: arXiv:2610.20032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contact-rich robotic insertion is challenging because uncertainty in alignment, friction, and contact conditions can lead to unsuccessful assembly, excessive contact forces, and jamming. Designing a reliable controller therefore requires balancing insertion performance, robustness, and recovery from unexpected contact. In this paper, we propose PSO+TR, a derivative-free optimization (DFO) method that combines the exploratory search of particle swarm optimization (PSO) with a trust-region (TR) procedure for local refinement to improve the search process when progress stagnates. We apply the method to derivative-free policy optimization of an interpretable robotic insertion controller, jointly tuning its motion, feedback, and recovery parameters while preserving its predefined control structure. The proposed approach is evaluated on 93 eligible benchmark problems from the bound-constrained programs (BCP) collection and a synthetic contact-rich planar insertion task under uncertain operating conditions. Three random seeds per benchmark problem yield 279 matched problem--seed instances per method. PSO+TR reaches the prescribed target on 228 of these instances (81.72\%), the highest observed target-attainment rate among the five compared methods, which also include PSO, randomized black-box optimization (VRBBO), matrix adaptation evolution strategy (MAES), and differential evolution (DE). Across eight robotic optimizer seeds, the deployed controller-selection pipeline achieves 97.78\% completion under development conditions and 58.00\% under withheld stress conditions, compared with 91.22\% and 31.12\%, respectively, for the fixed staged controller. The stress violation rate is reduced from 20.69\% to 2.19\%. These findings support combining global and local search for DFO and structured contact-rich controller tuning. The synthetic planar results require validation on physical robots.
item.dc:creator: Morteza Kimiaei, Roya Khalili-Amirabadi, Mohsen Jalaeian-Farimani

item.title: New Modelling and Solution Frameworks for Multiple Objectives, Decomposability and Impulsivity in Continuous-time Markov Decision Processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.20126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Impulsive control, in the context of continuous-time Markov decision processes (CTMDPs), refers to actions that instantaneously update the state of the process, leading to theoretical complications. Previous work has overcome these complications, but at the expense of approachability and ease of implementation: those models are mathematically complex and incompatible with pre-existing solution methods. This paper presents an alternative formulation of impulsive control for CTMDPs that is easier to employ in the modelling of real-world problems and can be solved by pre-existing solution methods. This formulation is then extended to allow for multiple objectives and decomposability. A decomposition-based heuristic method is developed that leverages Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition to find approximate Pareto fronts for large multi-objective decomposable impulsive CTMDPs. The modelling framework and solution methodology are applied to a dynamic maintenance problem to demonstrate their computational efficiency, solution space coverage, and solution quality.
item.dc:creator: Luke Fairley, Rob Shone, Peter Jacko, Jefferson Huang

item.title: Continuous-Time q-Learning with Nonsmooth Value Functions: a BSDE Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.20169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study continuous-time q-learning for entropy-regularized diffusion control without assuming classical differentiability of the value function. Rewards and admissible policies need only be Borel measurable, which allows discontinuous rewards. The diffusion coefficient $\sigma$ is action independent and locally uniformly elliptic, and the drift is $b_0 + \sigma\psi$, with $b_0$ action independent and $\psi$ bounded. In this setting the q-function involves the value only through its gradient. For each admissible policy, we represent its value by a backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) and prove that this value is continuous before the horizon, although the data are only measurable. Replacing the gradient with a measurable representation of the martingale integrand, we define the q-function up to Lebesgue-null sets and recover the classical definition when the value function is smooth. We then prove policy improvement, when the Gibbs update is admissible, and martingale characterizations of the value and the q-function from on-policy and off-policy observations. Here the candidate value need only be continuous before the horizon, and actions are sampled on a deterministic finite grid and held constant between sampling times. Under an integrability condition on the reward, we show that a second BSDE gives an upper bound for the optimal value, attained when its Gibbs policy is admissible, and we characterize its solution in the same way.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Asero, Elena Bandini, Andrea Cosso, Laura Perelli

item.title: Benign Degeneracy for First-Order Methods in Exact Boolean Moment-SOS Relaxations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pseudo-Boolean optimization -- minimizing a polynomial over $\{\pm 1\}^n$ -- includes MAX-CUT, binary quadratic optimization, and Ising models. The moment-sum-of-squares (Moment-SOS) hierarchy provides certified semidefinite relaxations that are often empirically exact at low order. We ask: once a relaxation is exact, how difficult is the resulting semidefinite program (SDP) to solve with first-order methods? Exactness does not imply regularity. At every order $d \ge 2$, a unique rank-one moment optimum is primal degenerate; moreover, if one optimal SOS certificate is strictly complementary, then the certificate set is positive-dimensional and contains singular boundary points. Thus first-order methods may converge to singular endpoints, around which pointwise analyses that assume regularity at the limit cannot establish a local linear convergence rate. We show that, for exact Boolean Moment-SOS relaxations in their canonical quotient form, this degeneracy is nevertheless benign. We develop an abstract mechanism, which we call residual-field rigidity, that propagates regularity from the relative interior of the optimal set to its singular boundary. For Boolean Moment-SOS, unique rank-one exactness and the existence of one strictly complementary certificate suffice to trigger this mechanism, yielding a uniform error bound around the entire optimal set. Consequently, exact ADMM, exact sGS-ADMM, and fixed-step PDHG converge eventually linearly from every initialization, even when their limiting certificate is singular. Finally, outside a lower-dimensional semialgebraic exceptional set of Boolean objectives, these hypotheses hold simultaneously at every uniquely rank-one exact order.
item.dc:creator: Shucheng Kang

item.title: Envelope Cubic Regularized Newton Method for Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.20345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problem $\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}\max_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ in which the objective has $\rho$-Lipschitz Hessian and condition number $\kappa$. We propose envelope cubic regularized Newton method (ECRN) which applies a refined inexact cubic regularized Newton method to the envelope of the primal function $\Phi(\cdot) : = \max_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}f(\cdot,\mathbf{y})$. We show that ECRN finds approximate second-order stationary points of $\Phi(\cdot)$ with $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt\rho\,\kappa^{3/4}\varepsilon^{-3/2})$ second-order oracles, improving the condition number dependence $\mathcal{O}(\kappa^{2})$ achieved by the best known second-order methods. Our improvement comes from the key observation that the Hessian Lipschitz parameter of the envelope is $\mathcal{O}(\rho\kappa^{3/2})$, which is sharper than the order of $\mathcal{O}(\rho\kappa^{3})$ for the function $\Phi(\cdot)$. We also conduct a lower bound on second-order methods to show that our complexity is optimal up to a logarithmic factor.
item.dc:creator: Qihao Zhou, Lesi Chen, Luo Luo, Chengchang Liu

item.title: On Partial Optimality in QUBO via Quadratic Posiform Autarkies
item.description: arXiv:2610.20346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partially optimal assignments (also called persistencies) allow combinatorial optimization problems to be reduced by fixing a subset of variables to values consistent with at least one optimal solution. For the quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, such assignments can be computed efficiently via autarkies of quadratic posiforms. However, the largest autarky domain and thus the number of fixed variables can depend on the specific posiform representation. We show that every quadratic posiform with the greatest possible constant term (the roof-dual bound) yields the largest autarky domain obtainable from any quadratic posiform. By computing such a roof-dual-optimal quadratic posiform and a corresponding autarky with largest domain in polynomial time, one can therefore attain the maximum partial optimality obtainable by quadratic posiform autarkies in polynomial time. This justifies the computation of roof-dual-optimal quadratic posiforms and corresponding autarkies in popular polynomial-time algorithms and establishes that finding additional partial optimality in QUBO requires going beyond autarkies of quadratic posiforms.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Fabian Naumann, Bjoern Andres

item.title: Dual-Inertial Bregman Methods with Energy-Based Safeguarding
item.description: arXiv:2610.20420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a dual-inertial framework for convex optimization that introduces inertia in dual coordinates while retaining the Bregman proximal-type oracles. For unrestarted iterations, uniformly bounded positive directional variation gives a last-iterate $\cO((1+\log k)/k^2)$ rate, improving to $\cO(k^{-2})$ under additional weighted summability. A computable safeguarded algorithm gives a global $\cO(N^{-1})$ objective-gap bound for the best accepted point, where $N$ counts all proximal oracle calls. Under local strong-convexity and kernel regularity conditions, all three safeguarded methods restart finitely and attain a final-epoch last-iterate $\cO(N^{-2})$ rate. Numerical experiments compare objective accuracy and computational cost on entropy regression and nonnegative least squares. Comparative numerical experiments illustrate the performance advantages of the proposed methods.
item.dc:creator: Kangming Chen

item.title: On the Complexity of Linear Programs with Parametric Constraint Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.20422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While sensitivity analysis for linear programs with parametric right- hand side vectors is well established, cases involving parametric constraint matrices remain less explored. To address this gap, we investigate linear programs where the constraint matrix depends linearly on a scalar parameter. Our goal is to compute the minimum and maximum optimal values of these parametric linear programs within a fixed parameter range. This corresponds to solving two bilevel programs. We show that both decision versions of these optimization problems are NP-complete by proving both NP-hardness and membership in NP. We additionally identify three sufficient conditions on the parametric matrix under which the bilevel programs are no longer NP-hard. We introduce a reformulation for both problems, together with a Farkas-based certificate for the lower-level feasibility condition, and compare the execution time for solving them on standard benchmark instances. The experiments highlight a practical dichotomy. Although both bilevel optimizations are NP-hard, computing the parameter value corresponding to the minimum of the linear program is fast, whereas computing the value corresponding to the maximum is not. We relate this asymmetry to the parametric equality constraints, whose free dual variables leave the relaxation of the maximum reformulation unbounded.
item.dc:creator: Laurie Boveroux, Margarida Carvalho, Andrea Lodi, Quentin Louveaux

item.title: A Decomposition-Based Data-Driven Branch-and-Bound Approach for Black-Box Global Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.20539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many scientific and engineering applications require the global optimization of expensive black-box functions. In high-dimensional settings, however, achieving computational scalability is a major challenge. To address this challenge, we propose a distributed spatial branch-and-bound framework that exploits partially separable structure for the global optimization of box-constrained black-box problems. The proposed framework adopts a two-layer structure in which branching is performed only on a lower-dimensional set of coupling variables in an outer layer. Within each outer node, the remaining non-overlapping (private) variables, which appear independently across blocks, have their domains partitioned and explored in parallel within an inner layer, resulting in a naturally parallelizable framework that is well suited for implementation on multi-core CPU architectures. At each node, valid upper bounds are obtained via sampling, with optional refinement using a local solver, while lower bounds are computed using data-driven convex underestimators constructed over partitions of the private variables. A residual-based correction and finite-sample validity analysis provide conditions under which the partitionwise underestimators are valid lower bounds, while the proposed branching and refinement mechanism establishes convergence to an $\epsilon$-global optimum. Numerical studies on benchmark and ODE-constrained parameter-estimation problems demonstrate improvements in both sampling efficiency and computational performance relative to monolithic approaches.
item.dc:creator: Damilola Fasiku, Wentao Tang

item.title: The quasi-convex Rockafellar theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.20542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rockafellar showed that every cyclically monotone operator is contained in the subdifferential of a convex function, and characterized the maximal ones. We establish the quasi-convex analogue of this theorem, with no assumption on the operator: in any separable Banach space, a setting we show to be sharp, every cyclically quasi-monotone operator is contained in the normal cone operator of a quasi-convex function. In finite dimension, we characterize maximal cyclically quasi-monotone operators and show that they are maximal quasi-monotone. Unlike in the convex case, the potential is not unique, and we build it from a preference relation obtained through successive preorders. As applications, we extend Afriat's theorem on revealed preferences in economics to infinite data sets, and obtain Kantorovich-type potentials for a supremal optimal transport problem.
item.dc:creator: Luigi De Pascale, Paul Pegon

item.title: Lag: A Mean-Field Optimal Policy for Online Assignment with Reusable Resources
item.description: arXiv:2610.19038v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study online task assignment with reusable resources. This problem arises in peer reviewer assignment, skill-based call routing, rideshare matching, emergency dispatch, and crowdsourcing: Tasks arrive according to a geometric process and must be immediately assigned to servers that become temporarily busy, yielding rewards that depend on the task-server pair. The goal is to maximize long-run average reward. We cast the problem as a contextual restless multi-armed bandit (CRMAB). We derive an occupancy-measure LP (OCC-LP) that upper-bounds the reward of any work-conserving policy. From its dual we obtain Lag, a closed-form index policy. We introduce a scaling regime in which the number of copies of each server and the number of arrivals per step grow together. This regime yields the first deterministic fluid limit for a contextual bandit. In it, Lag is asymptotically optimal. Finally, we evaluate our algorithms on peer review datasets and call center routing. The Lagrangian index achieves 83-99% of the LP upper bound across all load levels. Moreover, the Lagrangian index policy significantly outperforms the natural greedy assignment scheme, improving reward by up to 12.3% on journal data and 36% on structured synthetic instances.
item.dc:creator: Keerthana Gurushankar

item.title: Graph Coarsening Enables Escaping Local Optima in Compute-Constrained Nonconvex MAX-CUT
item.description: arXiv:2610.19043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Because its binary optimization landscape contains exponentially many local optima, MAX-CUT is highly sensitive to initialization. We study Particle Polynomial Relaxation (PPR), a moment-based nonconvex continuous reformulation possessing an advantageous optimization landscape. We warm-start PPR with Combinatorial Multigrid (CMG), a spectral graph-coarsening method that produces structure-aware initial solutions in near-linear time without training data. On \texttt{t2g20} ($n=400$), benchmark instance with known exact optimum, the combined CMG+PPR pipeline reaches $97.5\%$ of optimum on average and $98.4\%$ on the best run. An extended variant with discrete local-search refinement reaches the published optimum on all sixty Biq Mac instances evaluated by a recent neural branch-and-bound method. Using a sparse CSR representation, the same approach scales to G-set instances with up to $20{,}000$ vertices reducing memory requirements by up to $3333\times$ while maintaining a consistent improvement over the CMG warm start. Gains are largest on sparse weighted graphs; on dense graphs we complement the pipeline with spectral sparsification.
item.dc:creator: M. Harper Langston, Pierre-David Letourneau, Dalton Jones, Harris Teague, Peter Scott, Mingu Lee, Richard Lethin, Chris Lott, Roland Memisevic, Fatih Porikli

item.title: Long Term Pediatric Vaccine Tender Scheduling with Quantity Discounts
item.description: arXiv:2610.19045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pediatric vaccine procurement for low- and lower-middle-income countries (LICs and LMICs) requires long-term coordination across heterogeneous vaccine markets, competing stakeholder objectives, and uncertain demand, yet tenders are currently scheduled as a series of independent renewals. We extend the Hypothetically Coordinated Vaccine Market (HCVM) framework to schedule multi-year tenders with flexible lengths and all-unit quantity discounts, and compare three objectives: a balanced coordinatingentity model (UG), a social-benefit model that minimizes missed doses (SB), and a producer profit-maximizing model (MP). Using UNICEF ten-year demand forecasts and 30 demand replications across six discount scenarios, we find that the procurement objective, not demand variability, drives cost-to-tender and schedule complexity. Quantity discounts favor large producers, concentrating the market and increasing supply chain vulnerability. Discount effectiveness depends on market maturity rather than valency: pentavalent and hexavalent vaccines are already near their price floor, and among monovalent vaccines only rotavirus responds to discounts, whereas HPV and PCV remain too expensive to compete. Removing pentavalent and hexavalent vaccines from the procurement pool sharply increases missed doses. These results give planners practical guidance on objective selection, discount design, and protecting access to combination vaccines.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Uhorchak, Ruben Proano, Sandra Eksioglu, Burak Eksioglu

item.title: Full-Order Safety for Nonlinear Reduced-Order MPC
item.description: arXiv:2610.19250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reduced-order models (ROMs) make model predictive control (MPC) of high-dimensional nonlinear systems tractable, but the resulting modeling error can lead to constraint violations on the real system. We introduce CoRE-MPC, a robust MPC formulation that plans with a nonlinear ROM and guarantees recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction for the full-order system. It can be applied with a broad class of nonlinear model reduction techniques and the resulting MPC does not require evaluating the full-order model online, thus ensuring computational efficiency. The key insight is in how the ROM affects the dynamics of the prediction error. We account for this with two error radii that are propagated alongside the ROM and provide a guaranteed bound on the prediction error. The approach is validated in simulation on an 80-state oscillator chain, a Burgers equation, and a 9,768-state finite-element soft robot, where a two-state ROM with data-driven bounds keeps all 1,628 nodes clear of a wall at a median solve time below 1 ms for a 20 ms control period. Across these examples, CoRE-MPC is 13 to 61 times faster than full-order robust MPC at only 27 to 35% higher closed-loop cost, whereas existing certified schemes are either infeasible or at least twice as conservative. Code: [released upon publication].
item.dc:creator: Luis Pabon, Johannes K\"{o}hler, Revant Kasichainula, Marco Pavone

item.title: Maximizing Reaction via Spatial Localization: A PDE-Constrained Variational Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.19580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a PDE-constrained variational problem for the optimal spatial distribution of a catalytic material reacting with a substrate in a biological or materials system. With a given catalyst concentration, the substrate concentration is determined by a reaction-diffusion equation. The reaction functional for the catalyst concentrations is defined to be the total reaction output, which is the product of catalyst and substrate concentrations. Both the linear and Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics are considered. We construct reaction-maximizing sequences through the localization of catalysts using barrier functions and show the non-existence of a global maximizer. We also derive the first and second variations of the reaction functional. By constructing a competing catalyst concentration, we show the non-existence of a local maximizer. Based on our analysis, we propose a regularized variational model and prove the existence of its global maximizer.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Yasir Feroz Khan, Bo Li

item.title: C1 Virtual Element Methods for the Optimal Control of Oseen Equations with Stream-Function Formulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19662v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work analyzes a $C^1$-conforming virtual element method for the optimal control of generalized Oseen equations, formulated using the stream-function on simply connected polygonal domains. The method is based on a conforming discretization in $H^2$ of arbitrary order $k \ge 2$. The discrete scheme considers an approximation of the state and co-state equations which involves a specifically designed operator for the convective term and a \textit{variational discretization} of the control variable. We derive quasi-optimal a priori error estimates in the $H^1$ and $H^2$-norms for the stream-function, and in the $L^2$-norm for the control, under standard assumptions on the family of polygonal meshes. The proposed method recovers the fluid velocity, vorticity, and pressure using suitable projections. Finally, we report several numerical experiments to support the theoretical findings using different polygonal meshes including the cavity problem. We highlight that this analysis also covers OCPs governed by Brinkman and Stokes equation.
item.dc:creator: Arbaz Khan, David Mora, Alberth Silgado, Harpal Singh

item.title: Free-Material Optimization in a Peridynamic World
item.description: arXiv:2610.19776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study free-material optimization for nonlinear bond-based nonlocal diffusion and its localization as the interaction horizon $\delta$ vanishes. Bond conductivities are subject to pointwise bounds and a global material budget constraint. After normalization, the asymptotic behavior of these problems is governed by the fraction $\theta_\delta$ of potentially active bonds that can be assigned the maximal conductivity. We identify three distinct limiting regimes. If $\theta_\delta\to0$, the normalized optimal values converge to those of the classical vanishing-material optimal design problem, equivalently formulated as a Lipschitz-constrained state problem or a measure-valued flux problem. For $\theta_\delta\to\theta\in(0,1)$, we obtain a directional local free-material problem governed by the upper tail of the directional $p$-strain over position-direction space. Thus the state variable localizes, while the limiting constitutive law retains an internal directional variable inherited from the bonds. If $\theta_\delta\to\theta\geq1$, the limit is the isotropic local $p$-Dirichlet problem. A convex minimax argument eliminates the normalized conductivity variable exactly, after which the analysis combines convex duality, nonlocal compactness, and $\Gamma$-convergence for convex integrands. We prove a unified $\Gamma$-convergence result for the reduced state energies whenever $\theta_\delta\to\theta\in[0,+\infty)$, yielding convergence of normalized optimal values and compactness and identification of optimal states throughout the full parameter range. At the vanishing-material endpoint, we additionally recover optimal measure-valued local fluxes from optimal nonlocal two-point fluxes.
item.dc:creator: Anton Evgrafov

item.title: Online reduced-order modeling from primal solver trajectories for PDE-constrained optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.19821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Repeated high-fidelity state and gradient evaluations make large-scale PDE-constrained optimization computationally expensive. Reduced-order modeling provides a natural way to reduce the cost of these repeated high-dimensional computations. However, existing reduced-order modeling approaches often rely on converged high-fidelity states for model construction or updating, while their reduced spaces may lose accuracy as the design moves beyond the region represented by the available data. To address these limitations, we present Reduced-order Trajectory-based Optimization (RETO), an online framework that constructs local reduced-order models (ROMs) directly from unconverged primal solver trajectories. Each local ROM is built from snapshots collected during a finite number of high-fidelity primal iterations, without requiring full-order convergence, and supports multiple low-cost state evaluations, adjoint-based gradient evaluations, and design updates. New solver trajectories are generated at updated design points to reconstruct the local ROM and continue the optimization. Across three distinct PDE-constrained optimization problems, RETO achieves solution quality comparable to that of full-order optimization, with speedups of approximately 8 to 22 times in cases without discontinuities in the state fields. Even in the transonic inverse-design case involving moving shocks, RETO retains an approximately threefold speedup. The transonic results further show that the online local ROM progressively captures evolving shock-related flow features as new primal solver trajectories are incorporated. These results demonstrate the value of unconverged primal solver trajectories as an online information source for reduced-order optimization, allowing the reduced basis to evolve with the design rather than requiring a basis that covers the entire design space in advance.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Lu, Wenbo Cao, Weiwei Zhang

item.title: On the Optimisation Landscape of Overparameterised Weighted MMD
item.description: arXiv:2610.19861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the optimisation landscape of the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) over weighted atomic measures. For the one-dimensional Gaussian kernel, we show that, for any compactly supported target distribution, sufficiently many particles ensure that every local minimum has arbitrarily small MMD. Moreover, any stationary point whose MMD remains bounded away from zero is unstable under an unweighted gradient flow over the particle locations. These results hold both when the weights are constrained to the simplex, and when they are unconstrained but optimised at each step. When the target is itself finitely supported, we further strengthen this result: beyond an explicit particle threshold, there are no spurious local minima, and every spurious stationary point is unstable. To our knowledge, these are the first finite-particle overparameterisation guarantees of their kind for weighted MMD optimisation.
item.dc:creator: Tharrshann Jayan Logarajah, Jeremias Knoblauch, Louis Sharrock

item.title: Ergodic and Metastable Behavior of Stochastic Popularity Dynamics in Social Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.20021v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies popularity dynamics in social networks, where users' engagement with competing channels is driven by intrinsic content quality, social influence, and popularity feedback. We introduce a stochastic model in which users interact through a directed influence network and channel exposure depends jointly on these three mechanisms. We first characterize the resulting dynamics in the absence of intrinsic quality, showing that popularity concentrates asymptotically on a single channel, leading to a winner-takes-all regime. When all channels have positive intrinsic quality, we establish ergodicity of the popularity process and characterize its long-run behavior. We further show that, when intrinsic quality is small, the system exhibits metastable behavior: it can remain for long periods near configurations dominated by a single channel before transitioning to another. These results highlight how weak quality differences can coexist with strong path dependence induced by popularity feedback. We then investigate platform-level interventions and propose controls that compensate for network-induced exposure biases and mitigate excessive concentration. Analytical results are illustrated through numerical simulations and an empirical analysis of YouTube data, whose observed popularity dynamics are consistent with the proposed stochastic framework. The results provide a mathematical framework for understanding the interplay between quality, social influence, and reinforcement in online popularity dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Ravazzi, Paolo Frasca, Gaya Cocca

item.title: Routes planning in a condominium company using mathematical optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.20080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work focuses on planning daily routes for a group of employees of a condominium company. Given a set of employees and a set of customers with pre-scheduled visits, we want to build doubly-open routes to guarantee visits to all customers, ensuring that each customer is visited by an employee with the appropriate skills to carry out the required activity. The travel times between customers and the service time in each customer are known. The problem includes time windows for visiting customers, each employee has a maximum working time, and the daily working period is between 9 AM and 6:30 PM. The routes respect the lunch break period if they extend from morning to afternoon, which means that lunch break can be avoided if the route is fully completed in the morning or in the afternoon. The aim is to minimize the distance covered by all routes with a penalty for including lunch breaks. The distances and times between customers are collected via an API to Microsoft Azure; and the solutions are then displayed on Bing Maps. The results obtained show the operational advantages of an efficient and effective vehicle routing planning in a specific condominium management company. The model can be extended to other service provider companies.
item.dc:creator: Lara Rocha, Pedro Martins

item.title: An Analytic 0.48-Approximation for Non-Monotone k-Submodular Maximization under a Matroid Constraint
item.description: arXiv:2610.20140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a randomized polynomial-time $0.48$-approximation for maximizing a nonnegative non-monotone $k$-submodular function under a matroid constraint, for every $k\ge2$. The algorithm combines a top-two label rule with a nested-chain potential and maximum-weight matroid bases. Its analysis reduces the approximation guarantee to a one-dimensional time allocation: a uniform local lower bound leads to a linear differential equation, concavity closes the remaining interval, and two elementary budgets complete the proof. A strict saving in the time budget absorbs sampling and discretization errors, yielding the exact $0.48$ guarantee in the value-oracle model.
item.dc:creator: Zizong Wang, Yibo Wang

item.title: Dimension-Optimal Dynamic Regret in Exp-Concave Online Learning
item.description: arXiv:2610.20187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tracking changing comparators is a central problem in online learning. For exp-concave losses, previous work established the $T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3}$ dependence on the horizon $T$ and Euclidean path length $P_T$ for fixed dimension, while the optimal cost of dimension remained unresolved. We resolve this question by establishing a sharp $d^{1/3}$ curved dimension factor, improving the $d^{2/3}$ factor of recent switching and interval reductions [1, 2]. To achieve this improvement, we develop a proper, full-information learner on compact convex subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that adapts to the unknown path length and, under fixed dimension-independent diameter, gradient, and curvature parameters, guarantees $$\operatorname{Reg}_T(u_{1:T}) \le \widetilde{O}\left(d+\min\left\{d^{1/3}T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3},\sqrt{TP_T},T\right\}\right).$$ A matching lower bound on a diameter-one Euclidean ball establishes the minimax frontier up to logarithmic factors when $T\gtrsim d^2$, including the transition from the curved rate to larger path budgets. The lower bound already holds for losses that depend on only one coordinate per round, isolating an unavoidable cost of learning across directions. Our upper bound follows from square-root Gaussian KL control of comparator movement and a cancellation argument that pays for history restarts. The curved learner maintains $O(\log^2 T)$ Gaussian states, uses one gradient per round, and runs in time near-linear in $T$ under a Mahalanobis-projection oracle.
item.dc:creator: Yanyi Li, Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Qinshi Wang, Chenheng Zhang, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

item.title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
item.description: arXiv:2610.20413v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Momentum is a classical tool for accelerating convex optimization and a standard component of modern large language model training. Yet recent empirical work has questioned the usefulness of first-moment momentum in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We study this question through a bandit formulation of RLVR with bias-corrected exponential moving average (EMA) momentum, where the EMA coefficient $\beta$ controls how quickly the weights on past gradients decay. When policy gradients are evaluated exactly, we prove that increasing $\beta$ within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization. When gradients are estimated from sampled responses, a positive expected gain can be obscured by sampling fluctuations. We show that as the learning rate $\eta$ decreases, the expected gain with fixed $\beta$ vanishes faster than these fluctuations, whereas increasing $\beta$ to keep $\eta/(1-\beta)$ within the safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain that eventually dominates them. Bandit simulations quantitatively validate these predictions. RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base using SGD with EMA and AdamW support our principle of choosing larger coefficients in practical LLM post-training. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing $\beta_1$ improves mean validation accuracy by nearly $2$ percentage points over the conventional choice, demonstrating the principle's effectiveness at a larger model scale.
item.dc:creator: Kaifei Wang, Zikang Shan, Liwei Wang, Yinyu Ye, Han Zhong

item.title: Tracking a Small Set of Experts in Online Convex Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.20416v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the fundamental problem of prediction from expert advice, Freund asked whether one could compete with a comparator that switches $k$ times among only $m$ experts. For a discrete set of experts, this problem was resolved by Bousquet and Warmuth (2020), who gave an efficient algorithm with optimal regret matching the information-theoretic limit. We study the analogous problem in online convex optimization, where the action space is continuous. An inefficient algorithm can be derived by discretizing the action space and applying the Bousquet--Warmuth algorithm, giving regret of $\widetilde{O}(md+k)$, while the best known efficient algorithm for this problem has regret $\widetilde{O}(dk)$. We show that this computational inefficiency is inherent, establishing a separation between the information-theoretic and polynomial-time regret achievable for this problem. Specifically, under the hypergraphic planted-clique conjecture, we show that for every polynomial-time algorithm there exist instances for which it incurs at least $(k\sqrt d)^{1-o(1)}$ regret.
item.dc:creator: Angelos Assos, Anand Brahmbhatt, Elad Hazan

item.title: A Safe Approximation Based on Mixed-Integer Optimization for Non-Convex Distributional Robustness Governed by Univariate Indicator Functions
item.description: arXiv:2301.11185v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we present an algorithmically tractable safe approximation of distributionally robust optimization (DRO) problems that contain univariate indicator functions. The latter appear in different applications, but render the model nonlinear and nonconvex. The considered ambiguity sets can exploit moment information. Typically, reformulation approaches using duality theory need to make strong assumptions on the structure of the underlying constraints, such as convexity in the decisions or concavity in the uncertainty which cannot be assumed in our setting. We nevertheless present a semi-infinite minorant of the adversarial problem that admits a zero-gap dualization and is subsequently approximated by a discretized counterpart. Under mild assumptions, the latter provides a safe approximation that is a mixed-integer linear problem and can be solved by available standard software. Obtained solutions are guaranteed to be feasible for the original distributionally robust problem. We prove that the approximation of the adversarial problem converges to its true value for increasingly fine discretization, and that the values of the solutions of the safe approximations converge to the value of the true DRO problem under mild assumptions. In addition, the error bound yields an a posteriori enclosure of the true optimal value that can be evaluated in practice. On the practical side, the approach is made concrete for a challenging, fundamental task in material design, namely in particle separation. Computational results for a realistic setting show that the safe approximation meets the imposed quality requirement for every distribution in the ambiguity set, whereas the unprotected solution does not.
item.dc:creator: Jana Dienstbier, Frauke Liers, Florian R\"osel, Jan Rolfes

item.title: Geometric Certificates for Deterministic Global Linear Convergence of Overparameterized Projected Gradient Descent
item.description: arXiv:2403.02704v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study projected gradient descent (ProjGD) for the rank-constrained problem $\min\{f(X): \operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\}$ when the unconstrained minimizer $X_*$ has rank $r_*\le r$. Our main contribution is a quantitative geometric certificate relating the normal component of $\nabla f(X)$ to the smallest nonzero singular value of $X$. Under a rank-$(r+r_*)$ restricted curvature condition with constants $0<\mu<L$, every nonoptimal rank-$r$ stationary point satisfies $\|P_{T(X)^\perp}\nabla f(X)\|/\sigma_r(X)\ge [2L\mu/(L-\mu)]\sqrt{r/r_*}$, where $T(X)$ is the tangent space to the rank-$r$ manifold at $X$. This certificate implies that $X_*$ is the unique fixed point of ProjGD whenever the step size satisfies $\eta>\sqrt{r_*/r}(L-\mu)/(2L\mu)$. With an additional rank-$2r$ restricted smoothness assumption, we establish deterministic global linear convergence for $\sqrt{r_*/r}(L-\mu)/(2L\mu)<\eta<1/L$. The result accommodates arbitrary rank overparameterization $r\ge r_*$ and is independent of the singular-value condition number of $X_*$. As a consequence, we obtain an alternative proof of the sharp threshold $\delta<(1+\sqrt{r_*/r})^{-1}$ for the absence of spurious local minima in the asymmetric setting, where $\delta=(L-\mu)/(L+\mu)$. This threshold and matching asymmetric examples were established in recent work.
item.dc:creator: Teng Zhang

item.title: Global weight optimization of frame structures under free-vibration eigenvalue constraints
item.description: arXiv:2405.08894v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Topology optimization of frame structures under free-vibration eigenvalue constraints constitutes a challenging nonconvex polynomial optimization problem with disconnected feasible sets. In this article, we first formulate it as a polynomial semidefinite programming problem (SDP) of minimizing a linear function over a basic semi-algebraic feasible set. We then propose to solve this problem by Lasserre hierarchy of linear semidefinite relaxations providing a sequence of increasing lower bounds. To obtain also a sequence of upper bounds and thus conditions on global $\varepsilon$-optimality, we provide a bilevel reformulation that exhibits a special structure: The lower level is quasiconvex univariate and it has a non-empty interior if the constraints of the upper-level problem are satisfied. After deriving the conditions for the solvability of the lower-level problem, we thus provide a way to construct feasible points to the original SDP. Using such a feasible point, we modify the original nonlinear SDP to satisfy the conditions for the deployment of the Lasserre hierarchy. Solving arbitrary degree relaxation of the hierarchy, we prove that scaled first-order moments associated with the problem variables satisfy feasibility conditions for the lower-level problem and thus provide guaranteed upper and lower bounds on the objective function. Using these bounds, we develop a simple sufficient condition for global $\varepsilon$-optimality and prove that the optimality gap $\varepsilon$ converges to zero if the set of global minimizers is convex. Finally, we illustrate these results with four representative problems for which the hierarchy converges in at most five relaxation degrees
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Tyburec, M., Ko\v{c}vara, M., Handa, M., Zeman, J. (2026). Global Weight Optimization of Frame Structures under Free-Vibration Eigenvalue Constraints. SIAM Journal on Optimization, 36(3), 1647-1677
item.dc:creator: Marek Tyburec, Michal Ko\v{c}vara, Marouan Handa, Jan Zeman

item.title: Congestion-Aware Charging Coordination for Electric Ride-Hailing Fleets under Stochastic Demand
item.description: arXiv:2412.09978v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this study, we develop a dynamic charging scheduling method that integrates day-ahead charging planning and online reactive vehicle dispatch and charger assignment. The day-ahead planning model minimizes expected charging costs by considering anticipated waiting times and overnight energy replenishment costs. The online model then adapts this plan by maximizing the profit from vehicle dispatching and assigning vehicles to chargers through a reservation-based charging request scheduler to minimize the total charging-related operational time. The developed charging policy is tested on a Manhattan-like study area using synthetic data drawn from NYC yellow taxi data with a fleet size of 100 vehicles given the scenarios of 3000 and 4000 customers/day. The computational results show that our method outperforms different benchmark policies with up to +21.68% profit and +22.22% service rate for 4000 customers relative to the weakest benchmark. Sensitivity analyses are conducted for different system parameters, and managerial insights are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Tai-Yu Ma, Richard D. Connors, Francesco Viti

item.title: Exact penalty functions in optimization with unbounded constraint sets
item.description: arXiv:2507.03424v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper identifies necessary and sufficient conditions for the exactness of penalty functions in optimization problems whose constraint sets are not necessarily bounded. The case where the data of problems are {\em locally Lipschitz or semi-algebraic} is studied in detail. The conditions are given in terms of properties of the objective and residual functions of the problems in question. The obtained results generalize and improve some known results in the literature on exact penalty functions.
item.dc:creator: Liguo Jiao, Tien-Son Pham, Nguyen Van Tuyen

item.title: Linearly Convergent Algorithms for Nonsmooth Problems with Unknown Smooth Regions
item.description: arXiv:2507.19465v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop efficient algorithms for optimizing piecewise smooth (PWS) functions when their smooth regions are \emph{unknown} to the algorithm. For convex PWS functions satisfying a quadratic growth (QG) condition, we demonstrate that the bundle-level (BL)-type method~\cite{lemarechal1995new} achieves global linear convergence---to our knowledge, the first such result for any algorithm for this problem class. We extend the method to solve weakly convex PWS problems, achieving the same order of complexity as in smooth non-convex optimization. Furthermore, we introduce a verifiable and accurate termination criterion for PWS optimization. Like the gradient norm in smooth optimization, this certificate tightly characterizes the optimality gap under the QG condition and can be evaluated without knowledge of any problem parameters. We develop a search subroutine for this certificate and embed it within a guess-and-check framework, resulting in almost parameter-free algorithms for both convex QG and weakly convex PWS problems.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Zhang, Suvrit Sra

item.title: Predictive Control Strategies for Sustaining Innovation Adoption on Multilayer Social Networks
item.description: arXiv:2509.01457v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel compartmental model that couples adoption dynamics and opinion formation over a multilayer network, and we address an optimal control problem within this context. The diffusion of innovation is driven by social imitation through an exposure network and by the evolution of opinions resulting from social interactions. Individuals may temporarily abandon the technology or service due to dissatisfaction before reconsidering. The analysis of the equilibrium points and their stability allows us to analytically derive the necessary and sufficient conditions guaranteeing the persistence of adoption. Building on this result, we introduce a Model Predictive Control strategy that dynamically adapts interventions to the expected evolution of the system. We compare three classes of policies: influencing opinions, promoting adoption through direct incentives, and reducing dissatisfaction by improving the technology. Numerical results highlight the potential of predictive and adaptive strategies to support the sustainable diffusion of behaviors.
item.dc:creator: Martina Alutto, Qiulin Xu, Fabrizio Dabbene, Hideaki Ishii, Chiara Ravazzi

item.title: Risk-Aware LQR with Temporally Coupled States
item.description: arXiv:2603.23737v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate and solve a discrete-time linear-quadratic regulation (LQR) problem in a finite horizon thatpenalizes temporal variability and stochastic variability of the state trajectory. Our approach enables one to strike a balance between regulating the state and reducing temporal variability, with explicit sensitivity to risk. We achieve this by extending a risk measure called predictive variance to a setting with temporally coupled states. Numerical examples demonstrate the effect of temporal coupling in both risk-aware and risk-neutral control settings.
item.dc:creator: Chuanning Wei, Kin Fung Li, Dionysis Kalogerias, Margaret P. Chapman

item.title: $H^2$ Stabilization of the $2$-D and $3$-D Heat Equation via Modal Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2604.25909v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modal decomposition has been used recently to achieve boundary stabilization of linear parabolic equations in the $H^1$ norm, in two and three dimensions. In one dimension, $H^1$ exponential stability is well established and known to imply boundedness and asymptotic convergence of the state's max norm to zero. However, this implication does not necessarily hold in higher dimensions. In this paper, we prove that the modal-decomposition-based full-state feedback controller in \cite{Munteanu2017IJC} guarantees, not only $H^1$ exponential stability, but also $H^2$ exponential stability, which implies boundedness and asymptotic convergence of the state's max norm to zero. Our approach is based on rewriting the state's Laplacian, required in the expression of the state's $H^2$ norm, as a linear combination of the state and its time derivative. Thereby, the $L^2$ norm of the state's time derivative is the one to be analyzed in terms of boundedness and asymptotic convergence to zero.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Amine Ouchdiri, Mohamed-Camil Belhadjoudja, Mohamed Maghenem, Saad Benjelloun, Adnane Saoud

item.title: Symmetry-Compatible Principle for Optimizer Design: Embeddings, LM Heads, SwiGLU MLPs, and MoE Routers
item.description: arXiv:2605.18106v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A striking geometric disparity has long persisted in the practice of deep learning. While modern neural network architectures naturally exhibit rich symmetry and equivariance properties, popular optimizers such as Adam and its variants operate inherently coordinate-wise, rendering them unable to respect the equivariance structures of the parameter space. We address this disparity by introducing a symmetry-compatible principle for optimizer design: the gradient update rule should be equivariant under the symmetry group acting on the corresponding weight block. Following this principle, we first provide a unified perspective on bi-orthogonally equivariant updates for general matrix layers, as employed by stochastic spectral descent, Muon, Scion, and polar gradient methods. More importantly, by moving from orthogonal groups to permutation and shared-shift symmetries, we derive symmetry-compatible optimizers for parameter blocks whose symmetries differ from those of general matrix layers: embedding and LM head matrices, SwiGLU MLP projections, and MoE router matrices. These constructions include one-sided spectral, row-norm, hybrid row-norm/spectral, row-aware, column-aware, centered row-norm, and left-spectral updates. They yield an end-to-end layerwise optimizer stack in which each major matrix-valued parameter class is assigned an update whose equivariance matches its symmetry group. We corroborate this principle through pre-training experiments on dense and sparse MoE language models, including Qwen3-0.6B-style, Gemma 3 1B-style, OLMoE-1B-7B-style, and downsized gpt-oss architectures. Across these experiments, symmetry-compatible update rules consistently improve final validation loss, reduce expert load imbalance in sparse MoE models, and in several cases control final vocabulary-logit growth, improve router stability, and overall training stability over the corresponding AdamW updates.

item.title: Birkhoff interpolation models for optimization with some available derivatives
item.description: arXiv:2605.28503v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider interpolation-based derivative-free optimization in settings where only some derivatives are available. Such situations arise in scientific computing applications involving simulations, adjoint-enabled components, legacy software, or partially differentiable models. We introduce a Birkhoff interpolation framework that permits arbitrary patterns of derivative availability and enables the construction of local polynomial models using mixtures of function values and partial derivative information. In contrast to Hermite interpolation approaches, the proposed framework does not require all available derivatives to be queried at every interpolation point. We develop conditions under which the resulting interpolation systems are poised and establish corresponding model-accuracy bounds for fully quadratic interpolation models. We develop a trust-region framework that maintains poised interpolation sets while selectively incorporating derivative information. The method generalizes an established class of interpolation-based derivative-free optimization algorithms and naturally bridges derivative-free and derivative-based settings. We evaluate our approach on a collection of CUTEst test problems with synthetically generated derivative-availability patterns, as well as a stellarator design problem in which only some derivatives are available.
